model.architecture: Polaris-4B is an **RL post-trained reasoning model** built on Qwen3-4B (standard dense `qwen3`, Apache-2.0).

variants.quantization: blockwise int4 (block 128) + OCTAV optimal-clipping, embedding INT8, KV cache 4096, ChatML template

recommended.reason: the Android path verified on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24): full delegation (3274 ops across 2 subgraphs) and a correct answer to the probe; 9.2 tok/s decode, engine init 7.9 s, peak 1022 MB. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is the verified choice for the class, not a measured win over CPU

platform_notes: Reasoning model: set max-tokens >= 2048; truncated mid-thought it produces no answer.
Android GPU needs a ~12 GB+ device for this ~2.3 GB / 4B model; free RAM first on smaller phones.
block128 chosen over block32 because a 4B reasoning model's block32 weights can corrupt on the iPhone Metal GPU; block128 loads and runs stably across iPhone / Android / desktop.
Embedder externalized so every section stays under the iOS ~2 GiB single-section mmap limit; loads on iPhone.
Android GPU: XNNPACK takes 1 of 4 nodes in decode_embedder and prefill_embedder_128; the runtime accepts that split.
Mac CPU benchmark column is noisy (about ±7%); GPU rows repeat within about 1%.
Loads and runs on iPhone, Android and desktop; no iPhone or desktop on-device timing taken.

known_issues: Files downloaded before 2026-08-30 carried a SentencePiece-converted tokenizer that mis-encoded accented letters/symbols and mapped emoji and most Latin Extended-A to the end-of-text token. Re-download.
Accuracy figures and any on-device rows were measured on the previous (pre-2026-08-30) file; the on-device gate has not been re-run on the current file.
Prompts containing accented letters, symbols or emoji now tokenize differently from the previous file, so individual answers to such prompts can change.
